text.p: High-speed jetfoil ferry services between the Belgian port of Ostend and Ramsgate in England were suspended on Monday after striking mechanics blocked sailings, Belgian BRTN radio said.
The services by the Belgian state-owned Channel ferry operator RMT were expected to be on hold on Tuesday as well due to the strike, it added.
The 25 mechanics, responsible for day-to-day maintenance, fear the loss of premiums, which account for up to a quarter of their pay, and promotions once RMT ceases to exist.
In September the Belgian government decided to wind up RMT in 1999, leaving the Ramsgate to Ostend route to be run by Australia's Holyman Ltd and Sally Lines, a unit of Finland's Oy Silja Line AB.
RMT, hit by competition from other Channel ferry operators and the Channel Tunnel, has lost money every year since 1992 and has accumulated debts of 12 billion Belgian francs ($375.4 million).
The government forecast a 1996 loss of around three billion francs. RMT is expected to lose a further 1.8 and 1.6 billion francs in 1997 and 1998.
The government hopes to partly cover the losses by the sale of its ships and other assets. ($ = 31.97 Belgian Francs)
